top_comments.text:
Where does GROUND BEEF rank among your favorite animal proteins—🥇1, 🥈2, 🥉3, or lower? Drop your number below, then tell me your favorite way to prepare it! 👇

Ribeye gets the photo shoot. Ground beef gets dinner done. 😄

Here are the key sources behind this episode:

🥩 Ground beef versus ribeye nutrition
USDA nutrient database. We compared equal cooked weights—not equal raw portions. Values vary with the cut, fat content, and preparation.
https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/usda-national-nutrient-database-for-standard-reference-legacy-release

🔬 Minced beef versus steak: protein digestion
Pennings et al., 2013. In 10 older men, minced beef was digested and absorbed faster, but muscle protein synthesis did not significantly differ. This does NOT prove ground beef builds more muscle.
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23636241/

⚙️ Meat-grinder history
An original 1845 patent documents improvements to a sausage-meat cutter—not an established “first invention” of ground beef.
https://patents.google.com/patent/US3935

🍽️ USDA beef grades
Prime describes eating quality, including marbling—not overall nutritional superiority.
https://www.ams.usda.gov/grades-standards/beef/shields-and-marbling-pictures

🌡️ Ground-beef safety
Cook to 160°F using a thermometer. Color alone cannot establish safety.
https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/meat/ground-beef-and-food-safety

You don’t need a premium steak budget to put useful protein and nutrients on your plate. Keep protecting your NEST!

I have been disabled for 10+ years. Because of that my income is low enough to qualify for our local food pantry. Each month lately they have been giving out 2 of the 1# tubes of ground beef and usually one other option like pork chops, fish sticks, or some cut of chicken. This last month I got 3 huge frozen chicken breasts, each one weighed 1#!.
I know that is a big help, but since I eat Carnivore... 5#'s of meat only gets me 2, maybe 3 days out of the month. Idk if brakebush outlet stores are anywhere else, but there is one about 40 minutes away from me. My stepmom and I will ride together and stock up at the same time. I get a 10# box of chicken wings (unbreaded and cooked already) for like $12. I put those frozen right into my preheated air fryer and in less than 15 minutes I have a meal. Last time I went they also had a 20# box of already diced up and grilled chicken thighs for $20. Thats only $1/pound for grilled diced chicken thighs.
When I buy stuff at the store, I try to shop sales or bulk, and I look for pork loins to cut up into pork chops (cheaper per pound to just cut my own), or usually bone-in skin on chicken thighs are usually the cheapest by me. I love getting the skin crispy and chicken thighs with the skin are soooooo filling! 
I also have tins of sardines, mackerel, kippers, oysters, salmon, tuna, mussels, and cans of chicken. Tinned/canned meats are cheap, and the fish especially is very filling with all the fats... not to mention all the other benefits of the fatty fish.
Eggs are a cheap protein comparatively.
I also like the chuck roast. I just throw it in the crockpot before I go to bed, then when I am ready for break fast/lunch it is ready, plus I have the broth in there to drink as well, so I dont miss out on any of that collagen/connective tissue.
We have a local butcher who sells their meats at our farmers market for right at what the store sells it for, and sometimes its even less. And the best part is... they have a ranch right around here and they are transparent with who they use for their butcher. They are very nice and I support them as much as I can.
My tips I agree would be, buy cheaper cuts of meat, look for sales or bulk food stores, and cook them different ways so u dont get bored.
